about: Vectors for the x402/exact/tvm pairing: the tvm entry point of @integraledger/lcp. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2. The expected cell hashes, BoC and signature prefixes were computed with pytoniq-core 0.2.0 and PyNaCl 1.6.2; the request body hashes by a script that builds the settlement message with those tools and reproduces the vector's settlement root hash first. The payer's key is the Ed25519 seed 01 repeated 32 times. Negative settlement BoCs are V2's request with one part changed, except agreedRefusals' row 22, buyer row B6's settlementBoc with a bit set past the last byte in its last base64 character before the padding. Status fixtures model TON Center v3 answers: byInBodyRequest answers the lookup by the signed W5 request's body hash, byInMessage the lookups by message hash, keyed by the hash, byInBody a lookup by the Jetton transfer's body hash, which status does not make, and headUtime the masterchain head's gen_utime; each byInBody answer also names the gen_utime of a masterchain block through which its index holds every block, indexedUtime where the row gives it and the row's headUtime where it does not; inBody is a BoC in hex. Status counts only the payer Jetton wallet's transaction that took the message the payer's W5 wallet emitted in a transaction with the request: W5 checks the request's signature before any action runs (wallet_v5.fc). W5 refuses a request once valid_until <= now() (wallet_v5.fc), and an internal request that aborts leaves its seqno unused (wallet_v5.fc commits the seqno only for an external request), so the request can run again before valid_until: a lookup in which no transaction with the request emitted the Jetton transfer shows that the request never sends it only when its index holds every block through the head read first. A W5 transaction runs at its shard block's time, which a masterchain block references only later, so such a request reads failed only once the head read first is more than 60 seconds past valid_until. An internal message carries no expiry, so a request whose W5 transaction emitted the Jetton transfer is still in flight at any head.

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes where the pairing leaves the code to the implementation. The TypeScript and Python implementations both apply the option, build, complete and bound rows, the Python one the option rows through build. The advertise, recover and missing-peer rows are the TypeScript implementation's alone: the Python one has no advertise, no recover and no optional peer.

V2b.case: An undeployed wallet: build({…V2's choice, wallet: the state init's address, seqno: 0, stateInit: the base64 BoC}, H), then complete(signature). The internal message to the wallet carries init = the state init as a reference (Maybe 1, Either 1) and the signed body as a reference, as V2 lays the body out. The state init's code is a one-cell fixture (32 bits 0xdeadbeef); its data is W5's layout for the payer key: is_signature_allowed 1, seqno 0, wallet_id, the public key, no extensions. Computed with pytoniq-core 0.2.0 and PyNaCl 1.6.2 by a script that reproduces V2's settlement root 696775c9…1f15 exactly before adding the init.

nonCanonicalLibraries.case: V2b's choice with a state init whose libraries dictionary has a label that is not its shortest form: V2b's code and data, and one private library (the code cell, keyed by its representation hash) whose root edge label is hml_short, 514 bits, where hml_long, 267 bits, is the shortest. The wallet is the state init cell's representation hash, as x402's Python SDK 2.25.0 derives it (address_from_state_init). Parsing this state init and storing it again writes the label as hml_long, which is another cell (expectCanonicalStateInitHash), so build carries the cell as given: the request hash and signature are V2b's, and the settlement message's init is this cell. Computed with pytoniq-core 0.2.0 and PyNaCl 1.6.2 by a script that reproduces V2's and V2b's settlement roots exactly first. From global version 15 TON refuses to deploy an account whose libraries dictionary is not null (ton-blockchain/ton doc/GlobalVersions.md), so the row pins that build carries the cell byte for byte, not a wallet such a network deploys.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.
